title: Hypercohomology of a sheaf Hom complex into K-injectives
statement: Let C be a small category with Grothendieck topology J, R a sheaf of commutative rings, and A its category of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Assume a derived category D(A) [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let I be any endofunctor of integer-indexed cochain complexes in A [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules] whose objects I(M) are K-injective [def-pur-kinjective-complex]. There is an additive natural isomorphism, on the product of the opposite complex category and the complex category, between (L,M) ↦ H⁰(C,Q(Hom•(L,I(M)))) [def-pur-hom-complex] [def-pur-ringed-site-zeroth-hypercohomology] and (L,M) ↦ Hom_K(A)(L,I(M)), where K(A) is the homotopy category. The maps on the latter group are precomposition by L′ → L and postcomposition by I(M → M′). No resolution transformation, boundedness, or K-flatness of L is assumed.

source.place: Lemma 08JA (global assertion), using Lemmas 0A95 and 0A96 and Equation 0A8Z; source read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/08JA, /0A95, /0A96.

proof.text: For a K-flat source K and a K-injective target I(M), the sheaf Hom complex is K-injective by [lem-pur-hom-kflat-into-kinjective]. The definition [def-pur-ringed-site-zeroth-hypercohomology], via rightDerivedFunctorObjQIso and homologyFunctorFactors, computes its zeroth hypercohomology by the homology of degreewise global sections. This comparison is natural for maps between such complexes.

Use [lem-pur-hom-complex-global-cochains] to identify global cochains with the external Hom complex, respecting the signed differential. Build this identification from the chosen product projections [lem-sc-hom-complex-projections]; their map formula makes it commute with precomposition and postcomposition. Degree-zero cycles are chain maps and degree-zero boundaries are null-homotopic maps. Mathlib CochainComplex.HomComplex.homologyAddEquiv followed by CohomologyClass.homAddEquiv at zero and the shift-zero isomorphism gives the additive comparison with Hom in the homotopy category. It commutes with both variables because the chain-map representative is sent to its homotopy class.

For any source L choose a degreewise surjective K-flat quasi-isomorphism K → L by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. By [lem-pur-rhom-well-defined] the Hom-complex map Hom(L,I(M)) → Hom(K,I(M)) is a quasi-isomorphism, so applying Q and hypercohomology gives an isomorphism. Precomposition by K → L is also an additive isomorphism on homotopy classes into I(M): under [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] it becomes composition with an isomorphism. Transport the K-flat comparison across these maps.

Independence and naturality in L follow using common K-flat roofs. For two degreewise surjective K-flat resolutions of L their fibre product maps quasi-isomorphically to both, since each kernel is acyclic; resolve this fibre product again by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. The maps to both K-flat sources give equal transported comparisons by the naturality from Step 2. For a source map L′ → L, pull back a surjective resolution of L to L′ and take a K-flat resolution of that pullback; this gives a common roof and proves the naturality square. Postcomposition by I(f) commutes with every comparison and with transport. Thus the objectwise additive equivalences assemble into the asserted natural isomorphism. For zero complexes both groups vanish, and products support unbounded complexes.

lean.statement:
theorem homComplex_hypercohomology
    {C : Type u} [SmallCategory C]
    (J : GrothendieckTopology C) (R : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{u})
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u}
      ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)).obj R))]
    (I : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u}
      ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)).obj R)) ℤ ⥤
      CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u}
        ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)).obj R)) ℤ)
    (hI : ∀ M, (I.obj M).IsKInjective) :
    Nonempty (((𝟭 _).prod I ⋙ Functor.uncurry.obj (homComplexFunctor (R := R)) ⋙
        DerivedCategory.Q ⋙ ringedSiteZerothHypercohomology J R) ≅
      ((HomotopyCategory.quotient _ (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).op).prod
          (I ⋙ HomotopyCategory.quotient _ (ComplexShape.up ℤ)) ⋙
        Functor.uncurry.obj preadditiveCoyoneda)
